name: Living sunscreen
subtitle: skin bacteria that make their own sunscreen

effects.effect: the bacteria in the gut steer the body's immunity, weight and mood
a cell can run on a genome written entirely by computer

effect: the bacteria in the gut steer the body's immunity, weight and mood
how: Sunscreen only works when it is reapplied every two hours, which almost nobody does, and that is why skin cancer keeps rising. Algae and fish make their own ultraviolet-absorbing molecules rather than wearing them. A harmless skin bacterium that everyone already carries, given the genes for those molecules, would renew a thin absorbing layer by itself as long as it is fed by sweat, so protection does not wash or sweat off.
obstacle: Deliberately seeding an engineered organism onto skin that touches everyone else is a regulatory question nobody has answered.
why: The pigment genes are known; a living cosmetic faces an unsolved approval path.
real: Patents claim topically applied engineered commensal Staphylococcus epidermidis secreting the MAA shinorine as a self-renewing living sunscreen, and shinorine production has been engineered into Pseudomonas putida and cyanobacteria, but no in-use demonstration on skin was found (the living-sunscreen version exists as patents and an iGEM design project).
